run_metadata.coverage_summary: The environment's global egress block remains in place and was re-verified this run: WebFetch fails with DNS ENOTFOUND and a direct curl test returns HTTP 403 'CONNECT tunnel failed' for EVERY external host tested, including example.com, www.tenders.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au. The agent-proxy status endpoint reports enabled=true with no recent relay failures, so this is a deliberate outbound network-policy denial, not a transient fault - it cannot be worked around. Consequently NO tender detail page or specification document could be opened on any portal, and EVERY recorded opportunity is headline-level only (all counted in entries_pending_detail), with no deliverables/requirements/evaluation-criteria/documents/contacts extraction. WebSearch (routed via Anthropic infrastructure, not the egress proxy) was the only working tool; it is US-indexed and lags the live Australian portals. Despite that, this run surfaced more concrete, recently-published opportunities than recent runs: specific tender rows on buyer-originated portals - Gippsland Water (sewer/rising-main works, Buying for Victoria, opened ~9 Oct, closing ~17 Nov 2026), Ports Victoria (Station Pier fender upgrade, confirmed in the Ports Victoria FY26-FY27 procurement plan), and two buy.nsw rows (NSW Police radar technology RFP; a NSW community support services opportunity). CIS Tender 11 (WA, ~1.8 GW renewables, closing 22 Oct 2026) was strongly re-corroborated across multiple trade publications and remains open. Carried forward: the ACT Aquatic Strategy consultancy (closing 27 Oct 2026) and the two 2026-10-14 items (ABF Ship's Boats; Ron Barwick Prison), none of which could be re-verified on their primary portals. Tier 3 (mandatory) was checked - SAP Ariba Discovery and major-buyer portals (BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue, Woodside, Woolworths, Coles, Qantas, Telstra, banks) exposed no publicly-visible Australian RFx (all login-gated or invitation-only); their portals remain in discovered_sources, no corporate opportunities fabricated. Source discovery: six genuinely new buyer-originated sources recorded - Logan City Council (QLD), Wentworth Shire Council (NSW), Gunnedah Shire Council (NSW) and East Gippsland Shire Council (VIC), all now on VendorPanel, plus Ports Victoria and Gippsland Water as Victorian government-business-enterprise procurement channels.
gaps: EGRESS POLICY BLOCK (global, unchanged): the environment network policy denies all outbound HTTPS to external hosts. WebFetch fails with DNS ENOTFOUND and direct curl returns HTTP 403 'CONNECT tunnel failed' for every external host tested, including example.com, www.tenders.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au. Proxy status endpoint reports enabled=true with zero recent relay failures, confirming a policy denial rather than a transient error. Not retried per proxy guidance.

No tender detail pages, specification documents or portal listing pages could be opened on ANY source, so all eight recorded opportunities are headline-level only - deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, documents, contacts and exact closing times could not be extracted from primary sources.

WebSearch (the only working tool) is US-indexed and lags the live Australian portals, so Tier 1 portals (AusTender, buy.nsw, Buying for Victoria, QTenders, Tenders WA, Tenders SA, Tenders Tasmania, QTOL NT, Tenders ACT) could not be queried directly and mostly returned stale, already-closed or non-matching cached rows.

Gippsland Water opportunity: a Buying for Victoria search snippet gave tender id 'GW600' with internally inconsistent dates (opened 9 Oct vs 14 Oct 2026; closing 17 Nov vs 18 Nov 2026). The GW600 id could not be re-confirmed on a second search and the live tenders.vic.gov.au detail page is unreachable (egress block). Recorded at headline level with the most-cited closing date (17 Nov 2026) and flagged UNVERIFIED.

Ports Victoria Station Pier fender upgrade: the Ports Victoria FY26-FY27 procurement plan confirms the procurement exists (3-year contract, invitation to tender expected Q2 FY27 = Oct-Dec 2026), but the specific live tender id 'T421509' and the 30 Nov 2026 closing date came from a single WebSearch snippet and could not be verified on the live portal.

NSW Police radar RFP 'YR-2026-0040' (closing 10 Nov 2026) and NSW community support services 'PRJ_1584' (closing 27 Nov 2026) came from buy.nsw search-result snippets only; a second search could not corroborate either, and the live buy.nsw opportunity pages are unreachable. Recorded at headline level and flagged UNVERIFIED.

Carried-forward items 'ACT Aquatic Strategy Consultancy', 'Provision of Ship's Boats to the Australian Border Force' (AusTender) and 'Ron Barwick Minimum Security Prison amenities upgrade' (Tenders Tasmania) could NOT be re-verified on their primary portals this run (egress block); retained with original first_seen and flagged accordingly.

Tier 3 corporate: SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery and major-buyer portals (BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue, Woodside, Santos, Woolworths, Coles, Qantas, Telstra, Optus, TPG, CBA/Westpac/NAB/ANZ, AGL/Origin) exposed no publicly-visible Australian RFx via search; individual opportunities are registration-gated or invitation-only and were not captured as tenders (portals recorded in discovered_sources only). Invitation-only consultancy RFPs remain out of scope and were not fabricated.

Tier 1 states WA, SA, QLD and NT returned no live October-November 2026 opportunities via WebSearch and were effectively deferred; universities, TAFEs, CSIRO, public-health districts and most GBEs (water/energy/transport/ports) were not sampled this run and are deferred to future runs.
recommended_seed_additions: Gippsland Water (VIC) - government-business-enterprise publishing works/services tenders via Buying for Victoria (tenders.vic.gov.au); active sewer/rising-main works tender open now.
Ports Victoria (VIC) - GBE with a published FY26-FY27 procurement activity plan (Station Pier fender upgrade and others); monitor the plan plus Buying for Victoria for its invitations to tender.
Logan City Council (QLD) - moved all tenders/EOIs to VendorPanel effective 13 Jan 2025; no longer uses TenderLink.
Wentworth Shire Council (NSW) and Gunnedah Shire Council (NSW) - both now advertising tenders and high-value procurement via VendorPanel.
East Gippsland Shire Council (VIC) - major procurement moved to VendorPanel from Dec 2025 / Mar 2026; smaller contracts following.

Maintain a weekly VendorPanel Public Tenders sweep as the single highest-yield local-government channel now that NSW/VIC/QLD councils are consolidating onto it (East Gippsland, Logan, Wentworth, Gunnedah, Forbes, Narrabri, Mount Alexander, Camden, Temora).

tenders.title: Capacity Investment Scheme Tender 11 - ~1.8 GW renewable generation (WA Wholesale Electricity Market)
tenders.buyer: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW)
tenders.category: Renewable energy generation capacity (wind/solar) under the Capacity Investment Scheme
tenders.description: Commonwealth competitive tender under the Capacity Investment Scheme seeking approximately 1.8 GW of new renewable generation in the Western Australian Wholesale Electricity Market (WEM), with projects expected to be operating by 2030. Bidding opened 27 August 2026 and closes 22 October 2026, with successful bids to be announced March 2027.
tenders.eligibility: Reported to require participation in the independently-run Developer Rating Scheme (Equifax) - the first CIS tender to require it; developers must have commenced DRS assessment to bid. Projects must participate in WA's Reserve Capacity Mechanism. Full eligibility not verifiable (official DCCEEW page unreachable this run).
mandatory_conditions: Reported: participation in the Developer Rating Scheme (run by Equifax) required to bid
Reported: projects must participate in WA's Reserve Capacity Mechanism
Reported: includes a 180 MW First Nations Equity and Revenue Sharing Set Aside (>=5% First Nations equity or equivalent revenue-sharing)
tenders.reasoning: Carried forward from 2026-10-15; re-corroborated this run across multiple trade publications (pv-tech.org, pv-magazine-australia, esdnews.com.au, taiyangnews.info, enerdata.net, nsenergybusiness.com) all citing DCCEEW/the minister. Buyer-originated Commonwealth procurement channel (DCCEEW CIS, run with AEMO Services). Primary DCCEEW CIS page could not be opened (egress block).
tenders.notes: Headline-level only - no primary tender page or documents reachable (egress block). Closing date 22 Oct 2026 and design details (DRS requirement, First Nations set-aside, RCM participation, 2030 COD) are consistently reported across trade press citing DCCEEW/the minister but remain to be confirmed on the official DCCEEW CIS page / AEMO Services tender documents. tender_url, exact closing time, submission mechanics, value and contacts not published in reachable sources. Closes in ~6 days from this run.
